final_answer:
Using characteristics, write the incoming boundary trace

\[
w(t):=u(t,0).
\]

Then

\[
u(t,1)=w(t-1),\qquad v(t,0)=-b\,w(t-1),
\]

and hence

\[
v(t,3)=v(t-3,0)=-b\,w(t-4).
\]

The first boundary condition becomes the scalar delay difference equation

\[
w(t)=a\,w(t-1)-b\,w(t-4).
\]

For each fixed fractional time \(s\in[0,1)\), the sequence \(W_n=w(n+s)\) satisfies

\[
W_n=aW_{n-1}-bW_{n-4}.
\]

Thus exponential stability is equivalent to Schur stability of the characteristic polynomial

\[
p(z)=z^4-a z^3+b,
\]

meaning all its roots lie strictly inside \(|z|<1\).

Now apply the Schur reduction. For a monic real polynomial \(p\) with constant term \(c\), all roots lie in the unit disk iff \(|c|<1\) and

\[
\frac{p(z)-c\,p^*(z)}{z}
\]

has all roots in the unit disk, where \(p^*(z)=z^n p(1/z)\).

Here

\[
p(z)=z^4-a z^3+b,\qquad p^*(z)=1-a z+b z^4.
\]

First reduction gives, up to a positive factor,

\[
q_3(z)=z^3-Az^2+B,
\]

where

\[
A=\frac{a}{1+b},\qquad B=\frac{ab}{1-b^2}.
\]

We need \(0<b<1\), \(B<1\), and \(q_3\) Schur stable. Reducing once more gives, up to a positive factor,

\[
q_2(z)=z^2-\frac{A}{1-B^2}z+\frac{AB}{1-B^2}.
\]

For a quadratic \(z^2+Cz+D\), Schur stability is equivalent to

\[
|D|<1,\qquad 1+C+D>0,\qquad 1-C+D>0.
\]

Here this becomes

\[
\frac{AB}{1-B^2}<1,
\qquad
A<1+B,
\]

with the third inequality automatic.

Substituting \(A,B\), the nontrivial conditions reduce to

\[
0<b<1,
\]

\[
a<\frac{1-b^2}{\sqrt b},
\]

and

\[
a(1-2b)<1-b^2.
\]

The last inequality is automatic for \(b\ge \tfrac12\). Comparing the two active bounds for \(0<b<\tfrac12\), they are equal at \(b=\tfrac14\). Therefore the stability region is

\[
\boxed{
\begin{cases}
0<b<\frac14,\quad 0<a<\dfrac{1-b^2}{1-2b},\\[6pt]
\frac14\le b<1,\quad 0<a<\dfrac{1-b^2}{\sqrt b}.
\end{cases}
}
\]

At equality a root lies on the unit circle, so the inequalities must be strict. Thus exactly the pairs above give exponential stability.
